clinician.final_diagnosis: cervical myelopathy from spinal cord compression by arachnoid web
clinician.trajectory_summary: A man in his 60s presented with approximately 2 years of progressive spastic paraparesis characterized by worsening gait imbalance, frequent falls, back pain, spasms, and bilateral lower limb weakness without sensory symptoms. Neurological examination revealed hyperreflexia in all limbs, bilateral positive Babinski reflexes, a positive left Hoffman reflex, normal cranial nerves, absence of clonus, and preserved muscle strength. Initial spinal MRI demonstrated an arachnoid web at T7-T8 causing dorsal indentation on the spinal cord (positive scalpel sign) without syrinx. Clinical course over 3 months showed worsening gait, progressing from cane to walker use. Repeat spinal imaging including CT myelogram and thoracic MRI detected a possible arachnoid cyst at T7. These imaging and clinical findings led to neurosurgical referral. The progressive neurological signs, characteristic imaging findings of the arachnoid web/cyst causing spinal cord compression, and clinical worsening support the diagnosis of cervical myelopathy secondary to spinal cord compression by arachnoid web.
